package_info.package_manager: N/A (delivered as web content, not a package manager)
package_info.why_malicious: The entire kit is designed to create convincing fake browser login windows using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, with the intent to phish user credentials by mimicking legitimate SSO pop-ups and exfiltrating sensitive information to attacker-controlled servers.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (user interaction, e.g., clicking 'Sign in with Google')
execution_context.file_location: HTML/CSS/JavaScript embedded in phishing web page

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code displays a fake login pop-up window styled to mimic a legitimate SSO provider, embedding an iframe that loads a phishing page from a malicious server, resulting in credential harvesting.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This code creates a fake authentication window that appears identical to a legitimate SSO pop-up, but actually loads content from an attacker-controlled server.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal login pop-ups are generated by the browser or trusted SSO providers, not by arbitrary HTML/CSS/JS on a third-party site.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate sites may use iframes for embedding trusted content, but not for authentication pop-ups from untrusted origins.
key_indicators: iframe src points to non-official domain

execution_context.trigger: runtime (on page load or user action)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code listens for a user click on a login button and then displays the fake pop-up window containing the phishing iframe, facilitating the phishing flow.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This code programmatically displays a fake login window in response to user interaction, which is a common phishing technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate login flows use browser-native pop-ups or redirects, not custom-styled overlays triggered by JavaScript.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Custom modals for non-authentication purposes (e.g., help dialogs) are common, but not for SSO authentication.
key_indicators: JavaScript triggers display of fake authentication window
No browser security indicators (e.g., address bar, HTTPS lock)

attack_chain.action: User visits phishing site and is presented with a fake login button.
Fake pop-up window styled to mimic legitimate SSO provider appears, embedding a phishing page via iframe.
attack_chain.leads_to: User enters credentials into phishing form.

attack_chain.action: Credentials entered into the phishing form are sent to the attacker's server.

behavioral_signatures: Custom HTML/CSS elements mimicking browser or SSO pop-up windows
Use of iframes with src pointing to non-official authentication domains
file_indicators: Presence of .popup-window or similar classes in HTML/CSS
JavaScript code that displays overlays on login button click
network_indicators: iframe src or form action pointing to domains not associated with legitimate SSO providers (e.g., not accounts.google.com, facebook.com, etc.)
Credential POST requests to attacker-controlled domains
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for web pages that use custom HTML/CSS/JS to create overlays mimicking authentication pop-ups, especially those embedding iframes or forms pointing to non-official domains. Flag JavaScript that triggers display of such overlays on login actions. Analyze network traffic for credential submissions to untrusted endpoints.
